about: The free quota of each AI provider of AUTOMAT, as data (docs/MAINTENANCE.md, "The budget of the free quotas"). tools/ai-quota.py reads it; change a number here, never in code. Every number has its source. "verified": false means the number could not be checked against the provider's documentation on the day it was written: it is a conservative value (lower than what the provider is believed to allow), and the live rate-limit headers and 429 answers of each call correct the budget at run time. A person who checks a number against the provider's page sets it, with the date, and "verified": true.

reserve.source: tools/ai-review.py asks two independent providers (three for a tier-B change) once each; one review is the diff, the failure and the checklist (MAX_DIFF, FAILURE_SHOWN, ANSWER_TOKENS), estimated here at 9,000 tokens

share_source: the owner's request of 2026-11-22 (one candidate cannot drain a provider), narrowed by the owner's decision of 2026-11-24 (no fixed share for real updates: they get all of the quota): the half holds only while ANOTHER security fix or real update is pending at the same time, so two real updates share a provider fairly; a lone one may use all of it

priority.about: The owner's decisions of 2026-11-24: "use the free AIs every day, always when needed, above all for real updates; what is left goes to self-evolution, drills etc.", and: real updates may always use ALL of every provider's free quota, at any time; background work uses only what real work leaves, and all of it. tools/ai-quota.py priority_of() puts every piece of AI work in one of four classes by its branch: 1 security fixes, 2 updates of what ships to users (everything not named below: the engine and ad-blocking crates, Dark Reader, uBlock Origin's scriptlets, the filter lists, Python and Qt, the Breeze icons, the daily candidate, a fix of main), 3 updates of the CI and the tools, 4 background work (the AUTOMAT drill, the replay bench, self-evolution). Classes 1 and 2 are limited by nothing but the providers' own quotas (security first in the order of the work; share_per_candidate only while two of them are pending at once). Classes 3 and 4 run only while no work of class 1 or 2 is pending or retrying (an open pull request whose latest checks are not green, or a row of failures in AUTOMAT's memory of the last pending_days days whose newest pull request was not closed after it; never a long-lived branch such as automation/autofix-main), never while that list could not be read (fail closed), and only in a provider's leftover window: the last release_hours hours before its own reset (the time below, verified or not); for a reset not verified also never during the real day's maintenance_window (UTC); then they may use everything left. Each provider's use is counted on its own day (the time and zone of its reset).

maintenance_window.source: the real day's runs: security.yml 04:23, daily-check.yml 05:17, daily-maintenance.yml 06:17 UTC, then their tests and automatic fixes (several hours); until it is over the day's real needs are not known

priority.source: the owner's words of 2026-11-24; 3 hours, 2 days and the window are this repository's starting values, not the providers'

routing.source: a starting order only (strong: the agent that reads files and the largest context first; fast: the quickest answers first), unverified; tools/automat-route.py replaces it with the success rate AUTOMAT's memory records per provider and kind of task once a pair has min_samples attempts

Antigravity.what: Gemini's free tier, used by the Antigravity agent (one session reads and edits files in several requests) and by the reviewers through the Gemini API
Antigravity.source: requests_per_day and session_requests: this repository's own note of 2026-11-19 (.github/autofix/prompt.md: "about 20 model requests a day", "at most 10 steps"). The others: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits could not be reached on 2026-11-23; conservative values

Groq.source: tokens_per_minute: below this repository's own note (tools/ai-providers.py: "about 8,000 tokens a minute"). The others: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits could not be reached on 2026-11-23; conservative values

reset.source: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits could not be reached on 2026-11-24; Groq's own headers give the time to its next reset (x-ratelimit-reset-requests), which counts more; until a person checks it, the repository's own day (UTC)

account.source: every :free model of OpenRouter counts against ONE daily cap of the account, not one per model: 50 requests a day for an account that never bought credits, as remembered from openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits (not reachable on 2026-11-24). tools/ai-quota.py reads only is_free_tier of GET /api/v1/key (the address is tools/ai-providers.py OPENROUTER_KEY_INFO), with the key, at the start of each run that holds it, following no redirect: true confirms this value; anything else keeps it too, and the signing notice says the account is not on the free tier. The count of the day comes from OpenRouter's own headers and its 429 "free-models-per-day"
